summary: The gap register correctly names the core missing contracts (authority chain, topology ADR, narrow Release 1, cloud tenancy, collaboration, browser containment, static Page IR, tests, ops, supply chain, cost, handoff, UX, capability matrix, fallback sunset) and correctly withholds implementation authorization. It is not yet safe as engineering planning policy: the mandatory Grok 4.6 gate is unbounded, recursive, and certificate-like; audit packets have no data-classification or retention rule; live Git/GitHub/runtime snapshot claims are unavailable in this packet; and S0–S11 is not mapped to Page IR tickets, P1–P8, or current contribution/CI contracts. Correct the gate and evidence basis, then re-audit new hashes.

findings.targetSection: Review rule; §6 Mandatory Grok 4.6 stage gate; §7 Definition of Ready; §8 Definition of Done
findings.issue: The owner requirement that each named step is audited by exact x-ai/grok-4.6 is preserved in intent, but the mechanism is an invalid plan gate. DoR/DoD make a model PASS a necessary condition for Ready/Done, which elevates Grok from adversarial reviewer to process certifier despite the disclaimer. The gate applies to every S0–S11 stage, every ticket before work, every PR before merge, and every release candidate with no packet-size/context budget, no same-hash determinism rule, no independence rule against Grok closing Grok findings, no unavailable-model behavior beyond an undefined stop-the-line, and no emergency/rollback protocol that keeps the pin without creating an informal skip. That combination will either halt the website-first track or be waived in shadow process.

evidence.sectionOrLines: header Review rule; §6 Audit packet, Verdict rules, Independent verification; §7 last two Ready bullets; §8 Grok PASS and independent reviewer bullets
evidence.support: Pins x-ai/grok-4.6, forbids substitute models, preserves first REVISE verdict, and says Grok is not a certifier/authority; then requires Grok PASS before Ready, Done, merge, and RC with no packet cap, no reported-model mismatch fail, no same-hash replay rule, no retention/redaction, and no unavailability path other than BLOCKED.

Existing Page IR pack already has 25 reviewable tickets. Applying unbounded per-ticket plus per-PR plus per-stage audits without a scoped packet contract is not practicable and would retroactively unset status:ready.

findings.risk: False certification, self-review recursion, unbounded cost/latency/context, informal waivers, or a hard stop of already-authorized Page IR delivery.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Keep mandatory exact x-ai/grok-4.6 audit on each named S-stage, ticket, PR, and RC. Rewrite the mechanism: (1) Grok PASS is a stored review_input, never approval/certification; named human owner plus independent verifier remain the only acceptance voices. (2) Fail closed if reported model ≠ x-ai/grok-4.6. (3) Packet is hash-first: exact file list, SHA-256, bounded excerpts/diff, named receipts; no whole-repo inline. (4) One live audit per unique hash set; preserve first verdict; identical hashes reuse the stored verdict or dual-run both results and BLOCKED on disagreement. (5) Grok may not close Grok findings; human dispositions each P0/P1. (6) Unavailable model => BLOCKED, no substitute, no skip; owner may wait or stop-the-line; already-accepted S11 rollback runbooks may execute. (7) Record effort/usage/cost against EOS-012. (8) DoR/DoD wording: tests, independent verification, and human visual/release authority can fail closed even when Grok says PASS; Grok cannot override a failed deterministic check.

findings.issue: The mandatory audit packet stores raw request, raw response, diffs, test receipts, and candidate identity with no data classification, secret/PII prohibition, redaction, access control, or retention period. Making that packet a required gate creates a new external-model egress path for client evidence, run artifacts, prompts, and credentials that the local-API threat model does not cover.

evidence.support: Requires current diff or immutable candidate identity, tests/evaluations and raw receipts, plus raw request/response with no classification or redaction rule.

evidence.sectionOrLines: opening; upload/model redaction; ONE_BOX_API_TOKEN never in artifacts/prompts
evidence.support: Existing threat model is loopback single-user and already forbids secrets in artifacts/prompts; it does not authorize a mandatory third-party audit channel.
Cloud/privacy lifecycle is required before E0/E3/E6/P3, but the Grok packet itself is an immediate data-lifecycle path and is not listed there.

findings.risk: Required exfiltration of client facts, screenshots, transcripts, secrets, or private run state into model logs; retention of those payloads as planning evidence.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add a blocking audit-packet data contract before the gate is policy: deny secrets, env, sites/, .one-box/, OAuth, credentials, raw uploads, and client-identifying evidence unless the owner explicitly classifies a redacted excerpt as necessary; store hashes not bodies for binary/media; retention/access/deletion rules; redaction of prompt bodies in retained Markdown. EOS-005 must include this channel.
